proposed_comments.title: Use a publisher-controlled reverse-domain callback scheme
proposed_comments.body:
### Use a publisher-controlled reverse-domain callback scheme

**Severity:** `high`

The generic `cmdpal://` callback is not publisher-controlled and does not follow RFC 8252 guidance for native application callbacks. Providers that validate redirects strictly can reject it or treat it as untrusted.

```suggestion
- **CustomScheme** (`com.microsoft.powertoys.cmdpal://auth/callback`). The redirect reactivates Command
  Palette through its registered protocol, so the palette comes back to the front on
  its own. Only works with providers that allow custom-scheme redirect URIs, so it's
  the exception, not the rule. The Command Palette host registers this on the
  publisher-controlled reverse-domain scheme `com.microsoft.powertoys.cmdpal` per RFC 8252 §7.1.
```

confidence.rationale: The existing example is not a publisher-controlled reverse-domain custom scheme.

proposed_comments.title: Require expires_in and enforce device-code polling semantics
proposed_comments.body:
### Require expires_in and enforce device-code polling semantics **Severity:** `medium` The device-code example omits the mandatory `expires_in` contract and does not define required handling for `authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, network timeouts, or terminal errors. An implementation can otherwise wait indefinitely or poll incorrectly. ```suggestion Idp-->>Ext: device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval, expires_in Ext->>Page: Show user_code and verification_uri User->>Idp: Open verification_uri, enter user_code, consent loop Until expires_in or success Ext->>Idp: POST token endpoint
(grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code,
device_code, client_id) alt authorization_pending Idp-->>Ext: Keep polling at the current interval else slow_down Idp-->>Ext: Add 5 seconds to this and all later intervals else network timeout Ext->>Ext: Back off before retrying else access_denied or expired_token Idp-->>Ext: Stop with a terminal error else success Idp-->>Ext: access_token (+ optional refresh_token) Ext->>Ext: Optionally store the token and stop polling end end ```

confidence.rationale: RFC 8628 requires expiration and defined polling/error behavior that the current sequence omits.

proposed_comments.title: Bind authorization sessions to the initiating extension
proposed_comments.body:
### Bind authorization sessions to the initiating extension

**Severity:** `high`

The navigation contract describes a generic success signal without requiring session ownership or rejecting cross-extension completion. A leaked or replayed `SessionId` could otherwise complete another extension's flow and trigger its navigation.

```suggestion
The host navigates to your signed-in page for you, and only for you. You name that
page in `IAuthorizationRequest.SignedInPage` when you start the flow. The host checks
that the page belongs to your extension and holds onto it. After your token exchange
succeeds, the Toolkit calls `CompleteAuthorizationAsync(sessionId, true)`, and the
host foregrounds the palette and navigates to the page you already named. If the
exchange fails or the extension abandons the flow, it completes the session with
`false`, and the host clears the pending navigation without ever seeing a token.

The session deadline starts when the host accepts `RequestAuthorizationAsync` and
continues after the redirect is delivered until completion. When the deadline expires,
or when the extension disconnects or unloads, the host clears the retained page and
all pending broker state. The host binds each pending session to the extension that
started it and rejects completion requests from any other extension, even if a leaked
`SessionId` is guessed or replayed. Late, duplicate, or unknown completion calls fail
without navigating.
```

confidence.rationale: The broker contract lacks an explicit extension-ownership check for completion and retained navigation.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve refresh metadata and represent unknown expiry
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve refresh metadata and represent unknown expiry

**Severity:** `high`

A refresh response may omit both `refresh_token` and `scope`, and RFC 6749 also allows it to omit `expires_in`. Accept the previous `OAuthToken` rather than only its refresh-token string, preserve the prior refresh token and granted scope when omitted, represent expiry as nullable, and do not inherit the old access token's expiry for a refreshed token whose lifetime is unknown.

confidence.rationale: RFC 6749 permits omitted refresh metadata, and the current string-only API cannot preserve the granted scope or safely model an unknown refreshed-token expiry.

proposed_comments.title: Keep sign-in identity and navigation types host-owned
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep sign-in identity and navigation types host-owned

**Severity:** `high`

The host-owned sign-in UI must not display caller-controlled `DisplayName` text, because an extension could impersonate another extension or service. Derive the displayed extension identity from the bound manifest, use WinRT ABI types such as `IMapView<String, String>` and `IPage` for the request/result contract, and reuse the Toolkit's existing URL-launch helpers instead of adding a redundant host `OpenUrlAsync` method.

confidence.rationale: The host already has authoritative extension identity, and the current draft mixes non-WinRT collection/navigation types while duplicating an existing URL-launch capability.

proposed_comments.title: Complete the broker validation and error contract
proposed_comments.body:
### Complete the broker validation and error contract

**Severity:** `high`

The host contract currently promises only the happy path. Require S256 PKCE at the broker boundary, require HTTPS provider endpoints, and after validating `state` accept exactly one of an authorization `code` or a standard OAuth `error` while continuing to reject token-bearing and `form_post` responses. Otherwise denial can wait for timeout and malformed provider input can weaken the flow's assumptions.

confidence.rationale: The current security section does not define host-side PKCE or endpoint enforcement and provides no protocol path for valid OAuth error redirects.

proposed_comments.title: Document the Credential Locker same-user boundary
proposed_comments.body:
### Document the Credential Locker same-user boundary

**Severity:** `high`

CmdPal extension packages run as full-trust desktop processes, so `PasswordVault` is not an isolation boundary from the host or other processes running as the same Windows user. Describe it as at-rest/user separation only, make clear that namespaced keys prevent collisions rather than access, and require a stronger caller-supplied store or in-memory tokens when the threat model needs same-user process isolation.

confidence.rationale: The extension template uses runFullTrust, and PasswordVault documentation does not provide per-package isolation to non-AppContainer desktop processes.
